# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 10 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 10
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Moses said: "Do not eat swine, nor eagle, nor hawk, nor raven, nor any fish without scales." He was encoding three teachings in these prohibitions.
2. He also says in Deuteronomy: "I will make my statutes into a covenant with this people." So these commandments are not really about what you eat — Moses was speaking in the Spirit.
3. The pig: do not associate with people who resemble it — people who, when they are going without, forget about God, but when they are full, they remember him. Like the pig: when it is eating, it does not acknowledge its master; when it is hungry it squeals; when it is fed, it goes silent.
4. The eagle, hawk, kite, and raven: do not associate with — do not imitate — people who have no idea how to earn their living through honest work and sweat. Instead they take what belongs to others by force, while walking around pretending to be innocent, scanning for victims they can plunder. Just like these birds: they do not work for their food. They sit and wait and then devour what belongs to others. Predators in their wickedness.
5. The lamprey, polypus, and cuttlefish: do not become like people who are already completely condemned and godless — people who cling to this world as if it were something worth having. Like these fish: they are accursed, they do not swim free like other fish, they lurk in the mud at the bottom of the deep.
6. The hare: do not corrupt children, do not be like those who do. Why? Because the hare adds a new opening to its body every year, and so by the time it is old it has as many holes as years.
7. The hyena: do not be an adulterer or a seducer of others. Why? Because this animal switches sex every year — male one year, female the next.
8. And the weasel — hated with good reason. Do not be like those who, as everyone knows, commit unspeakable acts with the mouth. Do not keep company with women who practice filth with the mouth — because the weasel conceives through its mouth.
9. Moses intended all of this as spiritual commandment. But those who were enslaved to physical cravings heard it only as instructions about eating.
10. David also knew the three teachings, and he says the same thing in his own way: "Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, and does not stand in the way of sinners" — like the fish hiding in the mud at the bottom of the sea — "and does not sit in the chair of mockers" — like the birds sitting and scanning for prey.
11. There you have the teaching on food, in full.
